caption: What if India had no Himalayas? The range stretches about 2,500 km and is topped by Everest at 8,849 m. In winter, this wall blocks freezing, dry winds from Central Asia. Without it, north India would face much harsher cold. It also helps power the monsoon: a 2010 climate-model study found the mountain barrier keeps warm, wet monsoon air over India separate from cold, dry air to the north. Himalayan glaciers feed the Ganga, Yamuna and Brahmaputra, and the soil those rivers carried down built the fertile Indo-Gangetic plain that feeds hundreds of millions of people. Good news: the Himalayas are still rising, because India keeps pushing north by about 4 to 5 cm a year, roughly as fast as your nails grow. Plot twist: the rock at Everest's summit formed on an ancient seafloor about 470 million years ago, and it holds fossil sea shells. What would YOU miss most? 👇
